# Graft project — agent guide

Content is MDX in git. Postgres is a derived index. If they disagree, recompile.
Git wins. Day-to-day work uses the CLI and MCP. You do not need an admin UI.
Graft is open source and self-hostable (your Postgres, your object store).

- Schema: graft.config.ts (`defineCollection` / `field.*` over Zod). Single source of truth.
- Documents: content/<collection>/<slug>.mdx — frontmatter must satisfy the collection schema.
- Slugs are kebab-case. A frontmatter `slug:` overrides the filename.
- Compile: `graft compile` (once) or `graft dev` (watch). Needs DATABASE_URL in .env.
- One project = one database. Never point DATABASE_URL at another project's index
  (compile refuses with INDEX_OWNERSHIP).
- Primitives: `graft add <item>` copies owned source under graft/ and regenerates
  the graft/index.ts barrel. Run `graft add` with no name to list items.
- Assets: `graft asset put` or MCP `put_asset`, then reference `{ key, alt? }` on
  `field.asset` fields.
- Functions: POST /api/fn/<name> or MCP `run_function`. Mutations deny anonymous
  unless `public: true`. Destructive calls need human `graft approve` then retry
  with `approval` (MCP) or `x-graft-approval` (HTTP).
- Errors: every GraftError has a `fix` — do what it says, then retry.
- Docs: /docs/what-is-graft · /docs/getting-started · /docs/the-model · /docs/agent-surface · /why
- Ship changes as git commits. Every compile records the git SHA.
